note: The Byzantine Empire established a foothold in southern Iberia — the province of Spania — from 552 (when Emperor Justinian I exploited a Visigothic succession dispute) until 624 (when Visigothic King Suinthila expelled the last Byzantine garrison). Byzantine Spania controlled the coastal strip from Cartagena to the Strait of Gibraltar, including Malaga and Córdoba at its greatest extent. The Byzantine presence transmitted late Roman administrative culture, law, and artistic traditions to Iberia; the region's cities (Cartagena, Malaga) maintained their urban commercial character through the Byzantine period.

_quarry.structural_significance: Byzantine Spania is the last direct Roman imperial presence in the western Mediterranean; the province transmits Byzantine administrative and artistic traditions to Iberia; its eventual expulsion demonstrates that Byzantine reconquest strategy — occupying coastal enclaves — could not permanently hold territory against a unified Germanic kingdom
